$comment: Machine-readable registry of APR test suites and spec-requirement coverage. Verified by scripts/check-test-registry.py, which fails if a referenced fixture or test no longer exists, or if a requirement has no entry. The registry is a claim about coverage; the verifier is what makes the claim checkable.

gateStrength.gated: A test fails in CI if the rule is violated. The only level that actually holds an implementation.
gateStrength.partial: Some aspect of the rule is gated; other aspects are not.
gateStrength.indirect: Covered only through another component, not at this rule's own level.
gateStrength.external: Gated by a third-party suite this project does not maintain.
gateStrength.none: No test would fail if the rule were broken.
gateStrength.informative: Not a testable rule — definitional or explanatory text.

dimensions.completeness: Does the component do everything it claims?
dimensions.conformance: Does it agree with the format? (corpus + schema gates)
dimensions.correctness: Does it give right answers? (unit tests + coverage gate)
dimensions.robustness: Does it survive bad input and stay fixed? (edge cases, fuzz, mutation, regression)

suites.gate: schema agrees with every corpus fixture
suites.notes: Deliberately uses no .NET, so it fails the way a third-party SDK would.

suites.gate: ratcheting coverage (a floor, not a bar)
suites.robustnessNotes: CliRobustnessTests points empty, truncated, non-JSON, UTF-16, 50k-nested, binary and wrong-shape files at validate/info/stats. Contract: non-zero exit, no throw, no stack trace in output. Found that `info` exited 0 on any JSON object at all.

suites.notes: GUI suite runs (issue #30 fixed). Conformance is direct rather than inherited, and the project is now inside a coverage gate for the first time - it was excluded entirely while its GUI tests could not run, so there was nothing meaningful to measure. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
AT-SPI smoke test is manual, outside CI. No tests are skipped anywhere in the solution.
The only third-party conformance check in the project.
No tests of any kind. Implements a different schema.

suites.gate: the shared corpus, through the desktop view-model layer
suites.notes: Opening changes no response; a round-trip preserves documentType, version and unknown members; every prompt accepts any string whatever its hint; an invalid document still opens so the problem can be shown; a malformed one is refused; a tampered signature does not withhold the data.

suites.gate: every file under examples/ and tests/Fixtures/ must parse, validate, round-trip byte-stable, render through both PDF renderers unchanged, and satisfy the published schema
suites.notes: All 19 real form files - SF-86, IRS 990, IRS 1040, W-4, the bundled starter templates and two importer outputs. Enumerated from disk, so a new file is covered without being listed anywhere. The conformance corpus is synthetic by design, one rule per fixture; these catch what only shows up at the size and messiness of a real form. Found a shipped example that failed our own validator, and the editor bug that produced it.

testKinds.notes: veraPDF for PDF/A; cel-spec's suite available for the expression language now that CEL is adopted.

In-process automation-tree assertions run headlessly (AutomationTreeTests). External AT-SPI verification against a live application is still the manual script at tests/at-spi/run_at_spi_smoke.sh, outside CI. Two stubs that claimed to cover this were removed rather than left permanently skipped - a skip hides a gap instead of recording it.
Stryker.NET reports Killed:0. Until it runs, the 95% coverage gate is behaviourally unvalidated.

Deterministic mutation fuzzing of the parser (ParserFuzzTests): every truncation and 200 seeded single-character corruptions per corpus fixture, plus hand-built exhaustion structures. Fixed seed so a failure reproduces. Not coverage-guided - a real fuzzer (SharpFuzz) would explore further.
Vision targets 1000+ prompts under 1s; largest fixture is 20.
Requires two conformant implementations; only one exists.

requirements.statement: MUST/SHOULD/MAY are interpreted per RFC 2119
A different MAJOR version MUST be rejected
A newer MINOR version is readable, with a warning
A core-only reader MUST NOT reject a document using expressions, and MUST preserve the expr* strings
requirements.gap: Untestable from inside this repo: the reference implementation implements every profile, so it can never exhibit core-only behaviour. Needs a second implementation, or a deliberately profile-restricted test harness.

requirements.statement: A core-only reader MUST NOT reject a signed document, MUST preserve the signatures array, and MUST NOT report it as verified
requirements.gap: Same as REQ-2.2. A profile-restricted harness would be the cheapest way to gate both.

requirements.statement: Files MUST be UTF-8; a reader SHOULD tolerate a leading BOM
requirements.notes: Byte-level, because a C# string is already decoded and cannot express these cases. Asserts a leading BOM still parses, that UTF-16LE/BE are refused cleanly rather than mis-decoded, and that truncation mid-codepoint and arbitrary byte corruption are survived.

requirements.statement: JSON null is read as empty string and MUST NOT be written
A response given as a JSON number or boolean MUST be rejected at parse time
Any string is a valid response, whatever the hint
A hint MUST NOT reject, alter, or block a response
version and metadata are required; sections MUST contain at least one section
A filled form MUST record templateId
Section id and title are required; a section MUST carry content
Prompt label is required; a placeholder is never a label
A section and a prompt MAY share an id (separate namespaces)
requirements.notes: A section and a prompt both use the id "address". Without this fixture an implementation that pooled sections and prompts into one id namespace passed the entire corpus.

requirements.statement: Ids MUST be unique document-wide within their namespace
kind=table: children are instances, prompts correspond by position
At least 16 levels of section nesting MUST be supported
requirements.notes: Fixture pins the 16-level floor; the test walks up to the real ceiling (30 levels, set by System.Text.Json MaxDepth=64 at two JSON levels per section) and asserts the floor holds beneath it. The ceiling is recorded, not asserted - section 4.6 makes it an implementation detail that MUST NOT be relied upon.

requirements.statement: An unrecognized expectedDataType MUST degrade to text
The expectedDataType registry and every enumerated attribute value are published and consistent
requirements.notes: schemas/apr-types-1.0.json is the single published vocabulary. The .NET test asserts each type maps to the CEL type it claims; scripts/check-schema.py asserts the schema's examples and specification 4.7 name the same set. Previously these facts lived in five places.

requirements.statement: Unknown members MUST be preserved across a round-trip
Retired members are dropped, not preserved
Canonical write forms; every read form still accepted
documentType is authoritative over the file extension
The structural error list is exhaustive; no error from response content
Parse errors are not validation errors
requirements.notes: missing-required-members pins the shape the reference parser used to accept: an object with none of the required top-level members deserialized into a document of defaults, so `apr info` exited 0 on any JSON object at all while the schema rejected the same file.

requirements.statement: Strings MUST be NFC-normalized on read and write
requirements.gap: Preservation is asserted post-parse on both sides, so a read-time mutation of a fixture would not be caught for most characters.

requirements.statement: The abusive set is stripped; everything else survives untouched
Filled data MUST NOT be rewritten on the basis of a hint
submissionUrl hidden characters are reported, never rewritten, and block signing
Expression evaluation semantics: CEL, with expectedDataType supplying the type environment
requirements.notes: Conformance splits in two. The LANGUAGE is CEL, tested by cel-spec's own 2,456-test suite, which this project does not maintain. The BINDING - type environment from hints, unbindable values degrading rather than defaulting, marshalling back through the section 4.9 canonical forms - is APR-specific and is pinned by 12 published vectors.

requirements.statement: A computed field remains editable, and a correction MUST survive recomputation
requirements.notes: responseMetadata.source distinguishes a stale computed value from a human correction. Without it the two are indistinguishable and the next recompute silently reverts the correction.

requirements.statement: Signature required members; canonicalization MUST be apr-sig-v2; a signature MUST NOT carry its own copy of the submission URL
requirements.notes: The no-own-copy rule is enforced structurally: the field was removed from the model, and the re-signed fixture demonstrates its absence.

requirements.statement: The apr-sig-v2 canonical payload MUST be reproduced byte-for-byte
The payload binds metadata.submissionUrl, read from the document
requirements.notes: Closed a real vulnerability: verification once used a copy stored on the signature, so redirecting the metadata URL still verified.

requirements.statement: Editing covered content MUST invalidate the signature
Signature state MUST NOT gate parsing, validation, or data access
Labels and titles MUST be the accessible name; helpText programmatically associated
requirements.gap: The accessibility suite tests the desktop app, not the rule as a format requirement every renderer must meet.

requirements.statement: A section's own prompts render before its child sections
Export layout MUST NOT be written back into the APR document
requirements.notes: Serializes, exports to both PDF renderers, serializes again and requires byte-identical output; repeated export must not accumulate state either. A control case asserts two serializations with no export in between match, which is what revealed that the first failures were the serializer mutating the document rather than the renderer.

requirements.statement: A reader MUST bound nesting depth and SHOULD bound document size
requirements.notes: Fuzzed against every truncation and 200 single-character corruptions per corpus fixture, plus 50k-deep nesting, a 5MB string and 100k prompts. Exercised through both entry points, including DeserializeAsync(Stream) which is what actually opens a file. Contract asserted: parse either succeeds or throws SerializationException, within 5s - never an unexpected exception type to a caller told the format is safe to open.

requirements.statement: Reading a document MUST NOT fetch anything
requirements.notes: Asserted structurally: the core library references no System.Net type and links no HTTP client, so no input can cause a fetch. A behavioural test could only cover the paths it happened to walk.
